items.note: The word is most likely the Talmudic Aramaic karpada (cf. Hebrew קרפדה), so the spelling with ד is likelier. However, the preceding line's OCR shows ר in the variant קרפראי, so this is uncertain.

items.note: Tosafot Moed Katan 6b comments on Mishnah MK 1:4, 'צדין את האישות והעכברים' (one traps moles and mice), so the heading is צדין (they trap). צרין is an ד/ר misreading.

items.note: Joseph Schwarz's book, Jerusalem 5605 (1845), is titled תבואות הארץ, and the OCR has garbled its first word. Of the two readings, תוצאות ("outcomes, products") is the real Hebrew word and the closer misreading; חוצאות is not a word.

items.note: The previous line already gives the Talmud reading קרפראי (Berachoth 57b), so 'oder nach Aruch' must introduce a different variant. That points to קרפדאי, with ד/ר as the likely confusion, though I can't confirm Aruch's exact spelling.

items.note: תנשמת is the biblical bird name (Lev 11:18), discussed in Chulin 63a as a kind of bat. חנשמת is not a word.

items.note: The Aramaic word for 'bat' at Shabbat 78a is כרושתינא, which Jastrow also lists. In reading A the ת has been misread as the look-alike ח, which gives no real word.

items.line: emendirt werden in שורייץ קלבא שקורין עטלף שקורין, oder in חנשמת
items.note: Reading A, חנשמת, is not a word; it looks like a ח/ת misreading of the biblical תנשמת. Reading B keeps the correct spelling תנשמת, plus 'that is called' and the Aramaic name קלבא שוריץ, which fits an emendation of the Rashi gloss. But B spans several words, so it is unclear whether it matches the printed span exactly.

items.line: das doppeldeutige Wort in der Bibel, das gemeinsame Wort באוח
items.note: Chullin 63a identifies tinshemet with באותא (Rashi: the mole among the creeping creatures), spelled with ת, so B באות fits. A באוח is a ח/ת confusion and not a known word.

items.line: sich nur, wie חנשמת, das ebenfalls eine Fledermausart bedeutet und
items.note: The bird-list term is תנשמת (tinshemet, Lev. 11:18), so neither reading is exactly right. חנשמת differs by one look-alike letter (ת read as ח), which is a common OCR confusion. הנשמת would be a different misreading (ת read as ה), so the choice is a guess between two errors.

items.line: קיפוף „Das באות (d. i., חנשמת) unter den Vögeln ist קיפוף." —
items.note: The biblical bird name is תנשמת (Lev 11:18), and the passage spells it חנשמת throughout with ח, an OCR confusion for ת. Reading B, הנשמה ('the soul'), is not the bird name, so A is the printed form.

items.line: selbst übersetzt חנשמה zu Lev. 11, 18 und zu Deut. 14, 11 durch
items.note: The biblical word in Lev. 11:18 and Deut. 14:16 is תנשמת (tinshemet), here glossed as Fledermaus. חנשמה is OCR confusion of ת with ח and ת with ה, and is not a word.

items.line: Sabbat 78, a wird gesagt: „Das Blut der ברושהינא diene zu
items.note: Shabbat 78a names the bat כרושתינא, and its blood is used for an eye ailment. Reading A's ברושהינא shows typical ב/כ and ה/ת confusions and is not a word; B also gives the cleaner form of the disease name.

items.line: Ab. Sara 68, b wird der Unterschied zwischen עכברא דמהא (Stadt-
items.note: Lewysohn glosses the phrase as 'Stadtmaus', and the Aramaic for 'of the town' is דמתא (from מתא, 'town'). That matches the Talmudic contrast עכברא דמתא / עכברא דברא ('town mouse' / 'field mouse'); דמהא is not a word.

items.line: (עולה על שלחן מלבים). Raschi erklärt das Thier durch das Fremd-
items.note: The phrase is עולה על שלחן מלכים, "comes up on the table of kings", which matches "auf die Tische der Großen". מלבים is not a word that fits here.

items.line: ארנבת (Uxin 3, 3), ארנבא (Nedarim 65, a) und ארנבתא (im
items.note: The biblical and Mishnaic word for hare is ארנבת (Lev. 11:6, Uktzin 3:3). The list's later forms ארנבתא and the plural ארנבים fit a base ארנבת, and ארנבה is a ת/ה OCR confusion.

items.line: צמר (Menachoth 39, b) und mit Recht, da der Hase einen wolligen
items.note: The hair is called צמר (wool) in Menachoth 39b, ארנבת is the Hebrew name for the hare, and לנאי is the Greek-derived λαγώς form. Reading B's עמר, ארנבה and לגאי are OCR confusions (צ/ע, ת/ה, נ/ג).

items.line: Und dieses Thier wird sonst noch חגם (Targum zu Prov. 30, 26) und
items.note: Onkelos renders שפן (coney) as טפזא, so B's טפזא is right and A's טפוא is a ו/ז misread. חגס, with final samekh, is the Targum/Syriac form for Prov 30:26; that half is less certain.

items.line: בר טביא (Chulin 59, a), pl. צבאים (Kilajim 1, 6) und צבים (Sab-
items.note: Both spellings are possible: defective צבים/צביה and plene צביים/צבייה both occur in rabbinic texts. The passage text reads צבים and צביה, matching the biblical fem. צביה, so A is favoured, but this is a guess.

items.line: und אילהא (Bechoroth 7, b).
items.note: The Aramaic form of Hebrew אילה (hind) is אילתא, the word cited at Bechoroth 7b ('אילתא דמעברא'). The reading אילהא is an OCR confusion of ת with ה and is not a real word.

items.line: eines צבי דאין מצולות „eines Hirsches, der kein gegabeltes Geweih hat“,
items.note: Chulin 59b has 'tzvi de-ein karnav mefutzalot'. Lewysohn glosses it as 'kein gegabeltes Geweih', i.e. branching, which fits the root פצל. מפצלן ("branched") matches that meaning, while מצולות ("depths") makes no sense here.

items.line: עילאי רבי טביא „Hirsch des Waldes Ilai“ (s. §. 115) genannt. Das
items.note: Reading A looks like an OCR merge of the marked line's רבי טביא with דיין from the next line. Reading B, Rashi's Old French gloss for 'Daim', is a single plausible printed form, though the passage itself shows דייִן, so this is a guess.

items.line: גמליניתא חפשותא aus Μεγάλην (s. Artikel Maikäfer); doch kommt
items.note: Reading A gives correct word forms: חפשותא and גמליניתא, the latter a transposition of Μεγάλην. Reading B has ת/ח and ת/ה confusions (חפשוחא, גמליוניהא). The word order of A is uncertain, though.

items.line: noch die Angabe יעלה וו חשה (Jalkut Schim. 2. Th. fol. 122, c)
items.note: The phrase is יעלה זו ("this ibex"), the demonstrative זו followed by חשה, as in Job 39:1 midrash. "וו" is not a word here.

items.line: Thieres ist. — Raschi erklärt das Wort durch מושקא, Musc, den
items.note: Rashi's gloss is מושקא, from the Talmud's מושק (Musc, musk), so A's ק is correct and B's מושגא is not a word. The second word is less clear: A's משך matches the next line, but שמן ('Öl') may be what was printed.

items.line: heißt es כשב, כבש oder כבש; im ersten Monat des zweiten Jahres פלגם,
items.note: The Mishnah (Para 1:3) term for a sheep in the first month of its second year is פלגס (palgas), between כבש and איל. Final ם/ס is a common OCR confusion, and reading A also adds a stray כבש.

items.line: פלגם 1) von פלג „theilend“, d. h., zwischen כבש und איל stehend;
items.note: Mishnah Parah 1:3 names the animal between כבש and איל as פלגס (palges). The final ם in reading A is the common ם/ס confusion in Hebrew type. Lewysohn's second etymology, printed here as 'פלג גם', likely reads 'פלג גס' in the original, which fits the ס ending.

items.line: 2) פלג גם und פלג, wozu Maimuni: עדר הגדר, soll wohl heißen: עדר הגדול „groß-
items.note: The headword is palgas (Para 1:3). Splitting it as פלג + גס ('half' + 'large/coarse') explains the word, and it matches the following gloss 'groß'. The reading גם ('also') yields no etymology.

items.line: 2) פלג גם und פלג, wozu Maimuni: עדר הגדר, soll wohl heißen: עדר הגדול „groß-
items.note: Lewysohn emends the word to הגדול, so the printed form was probably the visually closer הגדר, a plausible corruption. הגרר is less likely, but both remain possible.

items.line: ברחא (Sabbat 18, b) und im Pl. עתודים, womit jedoch zuweilen un=
items.note: Talmudic terms are נדמה (B. Kama 77b, a hybrid birth) and שה פטרוזא (Bekhorot 11a), both in B. But עתודים in A is correct, not עתוזים, so neither reading is entirely right.

items.note: The parallel phrase קיסמא דחנון uses the genitive ד-, so קיסמא דריחמא (for דריתמא, 'stick of rotem', Shabbat 54b) fits best. But A could be an omission in the print itself.

items.note: Neither form is a word I can confirm for 'temple of the head' in Bechoroth 35a. טיפלש slightly better echoes the -s ending of Latin 'temporales'. This is close to a guess.

items.line: ten כבשים המצויירין שעורותיהן יפה בר' וה' סלעים „ausgezeichnete (bemerk-
items.note: The phrase means "worth four to five selaim" (בד' וה' סלעים). In Aboth de Rabbi Natan the text reads יפה בד' ("worth four"). Hmm, but the OCR word is בר' versus בד'. The prefix ב + ד' (numeral 4) fits "vier", so the printed word should be בד'. Correction: the choice should be B.

items.line: Verständniß. B. mez. 78, b wird erzählt, daß die Pelzmotte אבוקת
items.note: The Aramaic of B. Mez. 78b uses the determined form (cf. מילתא in the same sentence), so אבוקתא fits best. A dropped final aleph is not a typical lookalike-letter error, but it is still possible at line end.

items.line: hier erklärt Mussaphia מילח für den früheren Namen der Insel Malta,
items.note: The passage is about מילחא, milesian wool, and Mussaphia links the word מילח to Melita (Malta). Reading B, מילה, means 'circumcision' or 'word' and does not fit this sense.

items.line: und עיזין (Rabba Wajikra fol. 170, d); ברחה (B. Kama 48, a). —
items.note: עיזין is the regular Aramaic plural of עיזא, the form given just before. The doubled-yod עייזין is a possible plene spelling, so it cannot be ruled out.

items.line: abhängenden Ohren: גדיא חיוזא (Bechoroth 44, a). — Eine junge,
items.note: I lean towards חיוזא as the Bechoroth 44a term for a kid with drooping ears, as I recall a Jastrow-style entry for it, but my memory of the exact spelling is uncertain. חזיוא does not seem to be an attested word.

items.line: noch nicht trächtig gewordene Ziege: צפירתא דלא איפתח (Gittin 69, b).
items.note: The printed text has צפירתא דלא איפתח (Gittin 69b), followed by משכוכית (B. Kama 52a), the standard form for the lead goat. Reading B splits איפתח into nonsense fragments and drops the yod from משכוכית.

items.note: חיוי is a plausible Aramaic form here, and it sits closer graphically to Aruch's variant עיזי; חיי would more naturally mean 'life'. I could not verify the exact text at Chullin 43b.

items.line: Für חיוי ברייתי (Feldthiere Chulin 43, b) liest Aruch עיזי ברייתי „aus-
items.note: The plene Aramaic plural עיזי closely matches חיוי in shape and length, which would explain how Aruch's variant reading arose. Still, the defective spelling עזי is also attested, so B cannot be ruled out.

items.line: Haar heißt שער (Jebamoth 102, b), doch öfter נוצות, entweder weil
items.note: The passage line shows the plural נוצות for goat hair, which matches reading A. The trailing second word is unexplained in both readings, so this is not certain.

items.line: vorkommende מסריבן erklärt; hier aber wird bemerkt, daß dieser Rie-
items.note: The Shabbat 53a term that Rashi glosses as poitrail (breast-strap) is most likely מסריכן, with כ rather than ב. The extra second word (שנף/שטף) in both readings looks like OCR noise.

items.line: b). Unter שנף של עוים (Rabba Bereschit fol. 74, b), dessen Gestank
items.note: The passage is about goats (Ziege), and עזים is the standard Hebrew plural for goats. עוים would come from ו/ז confusion and gives no sense here.

items.line: Die vom Talmud erwähnte עוא דבאלא (Chulin 80, a) ist die
items.note: Aramaic for goat is עזא (cf. Hebrew עז). Chulin 80a reads עזא דבאלא, "wild goat", matching Lewysohn's Waldziege. עוא is not a word for goat.

items.line: 51). Das Wort באלא, welches in unsrer Stelle auch mit חור (Ochs)
items.note: Aramaic תור means 'ox' (the Talmud's תורבאלא, wild ox, at Chulin 80a), matching the German gloss 'Ochs'. חור means 'hole' or 'white' and does not fit.

items.line: בלא ברא für ברא (auswärts; so hält Bochart [Hieroz. P. I, lib. 3, cap. 1,
items.note: Bochart's 'Waldochs' is תורברא ('wild ox': תורא + ברא), and 'goat' is עיזא. Reading A's חורברא and עיוא are ח/ת and ו/ז misreadings.

items.line: §. 80) durchgehends: כרכין. Am wahrscheinlichsten ist hier eine locale
items.note: Reading A gives כרכין, Karo's variant, matching the passage, and כרכם, the Talmud's term (Kerkus). Reading B's ז-forms (כרכיז, כרכוז) are not words and look like ן/ם misread as ז.

items.line: כרכמיש soll aus כרך „Stadt“ und dem Nom. pr. כמיש zusammengesetzt
items.note: The etymology splits כרכמיש into כרך „Stadt“ plus the proper name כמיש (Chemosh), and reading A contains that full form. Its stray ם looks like an artifact from the next line's „Einschiebung des ם“. B's מיש lacks the initial כ, but its separated כ could be a word-order artifact of the same word, so this is not certain.

items.line: Sicherheit die gemeinte Species erkennen zu lassen. Die עיוא כרכם,
items.note: The Talmudic term (Chullin, cited via Shulchan Aruch YD 80) is the 'goat of Karkoz', עיזא (ד)כרכוז. Reading A's עיוא and כרכם are OCR confusions of ז/ו and ס/ם-type letters.

items.line: wird wohl mit עיוא כרכם indentisch sein; der Talmud zählt sie mit
items.note: עיזא is the Aramaic word for 'goat' (עיוא is not a word), and Chullin 80a discusses the animal עיזא (ד)כרכוז in this context.

items.line: letztres Thier niemals שור הבר, womit תאן identisch ist, heißt, vergl.
items.note: The biblical animal in Deut. 14:5 is תאו (te'o), which Lewysohn identifies with שור הבר. תאן is a ו→ן misreading of that word.

items.line: Tosephot (Sebachim 113, b. s. v. אורזילא): ואותם בופלש שאנו קורין ראם
items.note: Tosafot's Old French loanword is 'bufles' (buffaloes). Hebrew בופלש (bu-f-l-s) matches that form; בפולש looks like a letter transposition. This rests on the expected transliteration, not a checked edition.

items.line: noch Andere nennen ihn טור (Taurus) und דוביא (Lorje bei Alexander
items.note: Lewysohn glosses the word as Latin 'Taurus', for which טור with ט is the usual Hebrew transliteration. The passage line itself also shows טור and דוביא. תור is a genuine Aramaic form, though, and the doubled yod of B's דובייא is plausible too, so this is not certain.

items.line: Masc. שור und תור (Taurus, Sanhedrin 18, b), pl. שורים (B.
items.note: Lewysohn joins two cited plurals with 'und', so he must have printed two different forms. Reading A repeats the identical word, which makes no sense there. Reading B gives distinct plurals (שוורים and a תור-plural) matching the two singulars שור and תור. The exact second form is uncertain.

items.line: seinem Herrn als Freigut (הפקר) erklärte Ochs: שור המדבר (ibid.
items.note: The German text is about an ox ("Ochs"), so the word is שור. Bava Kamma 44b discusses "שור המדבר" in connection with a released, ownerless (הפקר) ox. שיר ("song") makes no sense here.

items.line: Jahre durch: תורתא, d. i., פרה. S. hierüber meinen Beitrag im L. Bl. d.
items.note: תורתא ('heifer/cow', Aramaic for פרה) is the Targum's rendering of Num. 19:2 (תורתא סומקתא). חורתא ('white one') does not mean פרה.

items.line: sant sind folgende Worte daselbst: אעפ"י שאמרו יולדת לט' יולדת לשלמים כבר חמהו
items.note: The phrase "כבר תמהו על זה רבים" means "many have already wondered at this" and is a standard rabbinic idiom. "חמהו" makes no sense here; ח and ת are easily confused in Hebrew type.

items.line: על זה רבים שהחוש מכויב זה והתו' כתבו שעתה נשתנו העניגים כמו שאמרו פ"ג
items.note: The phrase is שהחוש מכזיב זה, "experience (the senses) contradicts this". מכזיב (hif'il of כזב, "to belie") is the correct word here, while מכויב is not a word.

items.line: על זה רבים שהחוש מכויב זה והתו' כתבו שעתה נשתנו העניגים כמו שאמרו פ"ג
items.note: והתו' is the standard abbreviation for התוספות (the Tosafot), which fits 'כתבו' (they wrote) and the following citation; והתח is not a word here.

items.line: על זה רבים שהחוש מכויב זה והתו' כתבו שעתה נשתנו העניגים כמו שאמרו פ"ג
items.note: The phrase "נשתנו הענינים" ("the matters have changed") is the standard Tosafot formula. "העניגים" is not a word; it is a misreading of נ as ג.

items.line: der Hornzapfen (זכרות) endigt sich zwei, oder drei Finger weit vor
items.note: Reading A gives the real words: זכרות 'horn core' (Bechoroth 44a) and כרוכות 'layered' (Chulin 59b) both end in ת. Reading B's final ח is a typical ת/ח OCR confusion and yields no word.

items.line: ander zu kuppeln (רבקה, Raschi: קיפלא, Couple, Pesachim 26, a).
items.note: Rashi's Old French gloss for רבקה is 'couple/cople', which would be spelled with vav (קופלא); the yod reading is less likely. The sources are not checked, so this is not certain.

items.line: und אקורפיטא (Raschi: מניטורה s. §. 164). — Zum Stachel hatte
items.note: Rashi's Old French gloss for the manger is usually spelled with a double yod in the printed laaz. This is a guess; both spellings are plausible.

items.line: das zweibuckelige ist der generelle Name גמל, auch גמלתא (Rabba
items.note: גמלא, the Aramaic emphatic form of גמל, fits 'auch' as a generic variant and matches גמלא טייעא later in the passage. The feminine גמלתא is possible but less likely here.

items.line: bisches Kameel“ und גמלא פרסאה „persisches Kameel“ wohl zunächst
items.note: The Aramaic adjective 'Persian' in the emphatic state is פרסאה, parallel to טייעא, and this is the form attested in B. Kama 55a. פרסא usually means 'parasang' or 'Persia', so it does not fit as an adjective here.

items.line: Indessen durfte unter גמלא פרסאה vielleicht dennoch das zweibuckelige
items.note: The Aramaic gentilic 'Persian' is פרסאה (cf. גמלא פרסאה), matching the discussion of Persian/Bactrian camels. פרסא would mean 'parasang' and does not fit here.

items.line: beim persischen (B. Kama 55, a). Der Fettbuckel heißt חטרא, oder
items.note: The passage itself prints חטרא (Aramaic) and then חטטרת, i.e. חטוטרת, the camel's hump in Chulin 122a. Reading B's הטרת is not a word and wrongly uses ה for ח.

items.line: s. v. גרגרניות.
items.note: גרגרניות (gluttony, from גרגרן) fits the camel's voracity and is a plausible Aruch heading. גרדניוש is not a known word, though a garbled loanword heading cannot be fully excluded.

items.line: Dromedarweibchen ein Maulkorb (מזוי, Muselière) angelegt werden
items.note: Shabbat 51b uses זמם (muzzle, here spelled plene זומם) and אפסר (halter), which fit 'Maulkorb' and 'Halfter'. מזוי and אבסר are not words with these meanings.

items.line: b. Meier (רש"כם, zu Gen. 24, 11), daß unter dem talmudischen
items.note: Samuel b. Meir is known by the acronym רשב"ם (Rashbam), and he wrote the commentary on Genesis cited here. רש"כם is a ב/כ misreading and is not a word.

items.line: Pferd ist סום, סוסא und סוסיא (Megilla 16, a); doch heißt die mit
items.note: The Hebrew word for horse is סוס, which matches the forms סוסא and סוסיא listed with it; סום is a final-mem/samekh OCR confusion and not a word here.

items.line: מה"ח מערי מערב הפנימי, שהיה זמן רב בדרך ודקדק כמה וכמה פעמים
items.note: Both ודקדק and וידקדק fit 'and he examined closely'. The simple perfect with vav matches the surrounding later-Hebrew style (שהיה... והיה מונה), so A is slightly more likely, but this is a guess.

items.line: בשינה הסוס, והיה מונה נ"ט נשמי והסוס מתעורר, ועוד נ"ט נשמי והסוס
items.note: Before הסוס the construct form is needed: בשינת הסוס, 'in the horse's sleep'. The absolute form בשינה does not fit grammatically here.

items.line: (Raschi: אפוגרמט? A. Sara 11, a). Staatsverbrecher (Sanhedrin
items.note: The line has a single Raschi gloss, 'אפוגרמט?', on the hamstringing of the king's horse (A. Sara 11a). Reading B adds 'מתג רסן' (bridle, bit), which is foreign to this sentence and looks like intruding text.

items.line: grund hat: ארכביה אתרי רכשי „er läßt ihn auf zwei רכשי reiten“,
items.note: The Talmudic idiom is ארכביה אתרי רכשי, Aramaic א+תרי meaning "on two". This matches Lewysohn's "auf zwei". אחרי ("after") does not fit that meaning.

items.line: rachoth 58, a). Die Aviten (oder Gaviten) nannten den Esel תרחק
items.note: The Avite deity in 2 Kings 17:31 is Tartak (תרתק), which Sanhedrin 63b explains as a donkey. תרחק is an OCR confusion of ח for ת.

items.line: gen Esel heißen: עילי וטרא (Sabbat 155, a). Bemerkt sei hier schließ-
items.note: Reading B, which keeps the ז, is closer to the Aramaic זוטרא ('small'), the likely word for very young asses in Sabbat 155a. Reading A, וטרא, looks like a dropped ז. Neither reading is clearly the exact printed form, so this is a lean, not a certainty.

items.line: schrieben wurde (Berachoth 56, a). Für חמור findet sich auch חמורתא
items.note: חמורתא is the Aramaic emphatic/feminine form of חמור, the expected variant here; חמורחא is not a word and comes from a ת/ח confusion.

items.line: סיח übersetzt Raschi (Rosch ha-Schana 3, a) durch: עייר בן סום
items.note: The same passage later spells the word סיח (B. batra 78b), which suggests Lewysohn used the defective spelling here too. סייח (the Mishnaic plene form) is equally valid, so this is a guess.

items.line: סיח übersetzt Raschi (Rosch ha-Schana 3, a) durch: עייר בן סום
items.note: The gloss is „Pferdefüllen“ (horse-foal), so the word is סוס "horse" (עייר בן סוס). סום, with a final mem, is not a Hebrew word for horse.

items.line: (B. mez. 5, 4). — B. batra 78, b wird סיח durch מהלך אחר סיחה erklärt,
items.note: The gloss 'durch Zurufen des Treibers' means 'goes after speech/calling', i.e. שיחה (speech), a wordplay on סיח. The Talmud text may however spell the pun with ס, so A is also possible.

items.line: Esel ist selbst mitten im Sommer (בתקופת תמוז) kalt“ (Sabbat 53,
items.note: The phrase is חמרא בתקופת תמוז קרירא ליה (Shabbat 53a), meaning "in the season of Tammuz", which matches Lewysohn's "mitten im Sommer". בתקיפת is not a word that fits here.

items.line: trägt er beständig einen Packsattel (בשטיל, ital. Basto, Sabbat 52, b).
items.note: בשטיל matches 'basto' (packsaddle) through its s‑t sequence. בשמיל would need ט misread as מ, a plausible OCR confusion, but it gives no word fitting this meaning.

items.line: ist im Jeruschalmi (s. Simson zu Kilajim 8, 4) eine Leseart ניבדקם;
items.note: נובדקם is the נ-for-ל variant of the Mishnah's לובדקס (Kilajim 8,4), which fits Hitzig's 'Nubien' (with ו as in לוב); the final letter is likely ס in print, but both readings end in ם.

items.line: bat 51, b). Im Talmud heißt dieser Zaum פני דפרולא, was Schul.
items.note: The Gemara at Shabbat 51b likely names the Libyan ass's bridle פגי (פגי דפרזלא, an iron bit), which fits the Brechzaum gloss; פני ("face") makes no sense here. This rests on my memory of the passage, not a checked text.

items.line: ערוד (Kilajim 1, 6; Aruch liest auch ארוד), pl. ערודי (A. Sara
items.note: The passage is about the wild ass, ערוד. The Aruch variant is the same word spelled with aleph instead of ayin, so ארוד is the reading that fits. ארור means "cursed" and makes no sense as a variant spelling here.

items.line: Hüftknochen (אנקא, Hanche) sowohl der Länge als auch der Breite
items.note: I recall the Chulin 59a passage using אנקא for the haunch region and Jastrow glossing it as 'hip', though I can't fully verify either. ק and פ look alike in print; אנפא would mean 'face', which does not fit 'Hüftknochen'.

items.line: der Stamm des amalekitischen Bergvolkes mit den Worten: כערוד „der Südbewohner ununterjocht wie der Arod“ bezeichnet. Hier wird
items.note: The German gloss 'wie der Arod' and the nearby 'ערוד במדבר' (cf. Job 39:5) point to the plene spelling כערוד. The defective כערד is also possible in piyyut orthography, so this is not certain.

items.line: gabe der מקראות גדולות fälschlich בגו סיעתא ובאורדך lauten und בגו סיעתא
items.note: The marked line gives the Basel edition's 'false' reading. It must differ from the corrected form ובאורדך on the next line, which matches Landau's lemma ארדך. So the printed false form is ובאודרך.

items.line: Salomon Buber (in dem מגד ירחים 1. Heft. S. 48) liest אסיתא (Mörser)
items.note: אסיתא is the standard Aramaic/rabbinic word for 'mortar' (Mörser), which fits the gloss and Prov. 27:22 (במכתש); אסיחא is not a word.

items.line: glaube, daß das ו zu סיעתא gehört, ist aber aus ך-finale corrumpirt und zum
items.note: His proposed reading is סיעתאן, so the ו must be a corrupted final nun (ן), which also looks like ו. That makes ן-finale the printed form.

items.line: Die Maulstute מולאה, pl. מולאות (Mula, Sabbat 52, a), כורנייתא
items.note: The Aramaic for mules is כודנייתא (sg. כודנא), as in 'כודנייתא חיוורתא' in Shabbat 110b and Chullin 7b. כורנייתא is a ד/ר misreading.

items.line: (ibid. 110, b); die weißen כורנייתא חיוורתא und יימים, letzterer Name
items.note: The word is the biblical 'yemim' (Gen. 36:24, הימם), which Chulin 7b spells ימים and the Midrash explains as Ἡμίονος, 'mule'. The doubled yod in יימים is not a word and is an OCR artifact.

items.line: 79, a); das Weibchen: פרדה (ibid.). Das Junge: גירדונא ווטרתא
items.note: Reading A is more likely printed. Buxtorf's variant is glossed with Greek Γαιδαρο, whose g‑d‑r order fits גידרונא, so the Talmud text cited would be the different form גירדונא. ווטרתא with ת is the natural spelling, while ח looks like an OCR slip. The next line's OCR of Buxtorf's form is itself doubtful, so this is not certain.

items.line: כורנייתא der Name für פרד ist. — Von פרד ist der Pl. פרדים (Jo-
items.note: The Aramaic word for mule is כודנא (kudna), with plural כודנייתא, and this is the form found in the Talmudic context the Tosafot discuss. כורנייתא is not an attested word, so it is a ד/ר OCR confusion.

items.line: kinderlosen Ehegatten sprüchwörtlich: כורנא עקרה „unfruchtbare Maul-
items.note: The Aramaic word for a mule (Maulstute) is כודנא / כודניתא. The Bava Batra 91a phrase is כודנא עקרה, 'barren mule'. כורנא is not the mule word, so the ר is a misreading of ד.

items.line: חית נכר „das wühlende Thier“; vgl. hierzu B. Kama 17, b.
items.note: B's נבר ('to burrow, root', cf. B. Kama 17b, a pig rooting in a dunghill) fits 'das wühlende Thier', and פיסתקא with ת is the likely form. But B's French gloss גלו"נש looks garbled, and A's גלנ"ש fits 'Glands' better, so the readings are mixed.

items.line: Schweines ist mannigfach. Getrockneter Schinken (Raschi: בקנוש,
items.note: Rashi's la'az on Chulin 17a for dried pork is Old French 'bacons', transliterated בקונש with vav after qof for the 'o'. בקנוש misplaces the vowel letter and is not the known gloss.

items.line: رئم, eine Gazellenart bezeichnet, sondern auch der Talmud ארוילא,
items.note: The Talmudic word for ראם is ארזילא / אורזילא (Zevachim 113b), which Lewysohn links to Arabic غزال. Reading A matches this letter-for-letter with ז misread as ו. Reading B scrambles the order and drops a letter. Neither reading is exactly the printed form, so this is not certain.

items.line: durch Elfenbein (איבויירא. Ivoire).
items.note: איבויירא fits Old French 'ivoire' better: the vav renders the o. Reading B drops that vowel, but Rashi's loanword spellings vary, so this is not certain.

items.line: in dieser Stelle werden auch die biblischen חנינים הגרולים (Meerunge-
items.note: Reading B, התנינים הגדולים (Gen 1:21, 'the great sea monsters'), is the correct word. Reading A has הגרולים, a ד/ר confusion that gives a non-word, and it also lacks the article ה.

items.line: 2. Th. §. 845 קרנותיו vom Reem vorkommt, doch ist unsere Aufgabe
items.note: Yalkut Shimoni is a Hebrew midrash, so the Hebrew plural with suffix, קרנותיו ('his horns'), fits the reem passage better than Aramaic קרנוהי. Both forms are possible words, so this is not certain.

items.line: קרס (§. 146) sich geirrt hat. — Unser Thier wird auch von Aelian
items.note: Here Lewysohn is discussing one-horned animals. The Talmudic keresh (קרש, Chullin 59b) is the animal said to have a single horn, which fits the cross-reference to §. 146. The reading קרס (hook or clasp) is not an animal name.

items.line: Bechoroth 8, a heißt es: Die דולפנין (Delphine) vermehren sich
items.note: The Talmud at Bechoroth 8a spells it הדולפנין. The same passage repeats דולפנין and transliterates it 'Dulphenin', with no yod after the פ. The extra yod in B looks like an OCR insertion.

items.line: mud, was דולפנין wären, welche Frage Rabbi Jehuda mit den Wor-
items.note: The earlier line of the same passage prints דולפנין, and the transliteration 'Dulphenin' fits that spelling, so Lewysohn was likely consistent. The standard Talmud text of Bechoroth 8a reads דולפינין, though, so B is also plausible.

items.line: sich nähernde Aehnlichkeit mit dem Hunde; כלביה ist vielmehr der
items.note: The Talmudic fish-name, rendered by Jastrow as a dog-fish (Ab. Zar. 40a), is כלבית. Reading A's final ה looks like the common ת/ה confusion. Reading B's one variant כלכית is a ב/כ slip.

items.line: So heißt es auch vom Liviatan im Piut s. v. חשורת שי zum 2. Tag
items.note: The piyut incipit is 'תשורת שי' ('gift of tribute', after תשורה in 1 Sam 9:7). 'חשורת' gives no sense in this phrase; ח/ת is a common OCR confusion.

items.line: Succoth: לקשור לוית צלצל דנתי.
items.note: The piyyut line echoes Job 40:31, "בצלצל דגים" (the fish-spear used against Leviathan), so a form built on דג/דגה (fish) fits. דנתי makes little sense here, but the exact piyyut wording is not verified.

items.line: die Muränen (מרנס, Muraenae), welche man in dem רג בלי"נא fin-
items.note: B gives דג ('fish'), which fits 'the fish called balaena', whereas רג is a ד/ר misreading. B's בליינא is also plausible. Whether the Old French gloss is מרנש or מרנס is uncertain, so the choice rests mainly on דג.

items.line: Räucherwerk im Tempel bestand. Zu diesen wurde auch von dem כיפה
items.note: The incense list in Keritot 6a reads "כיפת הירדן", a construct form ending in ת, which fits "הירדן" following it. Reading A, "כיפה", is the absolute form and does not fit the construct here.

items.line: רעי של רג הגדל בירדן והוא עמכרא. Sollten diese Worte den Sinn
items.note: The gloss "Excremente des großen Fisches" requires דג (fish), so the phrase is רעי של דג הגדל. רג is not a word that fits here.

items.line: רעי של רג הגדל בירדן והוא עמכרא. Sollten diese Worte den Sinn
items.note: The passage glosses the word as 'Ambra' (ambergris), so it should read עמברא, Arabic 'anbar. עמכרא is a ב/כ misreading and is not a word.
